from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Review: From Arrows to Rules", [
            "Vectors are arrows with length and direction.",
            "They follow specific algebraic rules.",
            "Addition and scaling are fundamental."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        arrow = Vector(direction=RIGHT*1.5 + UP*1.5, color="#FF5733")
        self.place_at_grid(arrow, 'C3')
        self.play(Create(arrow))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF5733")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            arrow.animate.scale(1.5).rotate(PI/4),
            run_time=2
        )
        arrow.set_color("#33FF57")
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#33FF57")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        dot = Dot(color="#3357FF")
        self.place_at_grid(dot, 'D4')
        self.play(
            FadeOut(arrow),
            FadeIn(dot),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#3357FF")
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "A vector space is a collection of objects.",
            "It satisfies eight fundamental axioms.",
            "Vectors aren't just physical arrows.",
            "Functions can be vectors.",
            "Polynomials can be vectors too."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Generalization Leap", lecture_lines)
        
        # Assets

        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF5733")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Application: The Library of Sounds", [
            "Audio signals can be vectors.", 
            "Each time point is a dimension.", 
            "Adding clips creates a new sound.", 
            "This represents signal superposition.", 
            "Abstraction simplifies complex sound analysis."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Audio signals can be vectors.
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF5733")
        wave = Line(LEFT, RIGHT, color="#FF5733").set_length(4)
        self.place_at_grid(wave, 'C3')
        self.play(Create(wave))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Each time point is a dimension.
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF5733")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Adding clips creates a new sound.
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF33FF")
        bass = Arrow(ORIGIN, UP*1.5, color="#33FF57", buff=0)
        treble = Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT*1.5, color="#3357FF", buff=0)
        
        bass_label = Text("Bass", font_size=20, color="#33FF57")
        treble_label = Text("Treble", font_size=20, color="#3357FF")
        
        bass_group = VGroup(bass, bass_label).arrange(UP)
        treble_group = VGroup(treble, treble_label).arrange(RIGHT)
        
        self.place_at_grid(bass_group, 'B2')
        self.place_at_grid(treble_group, 'B4')
        self.play(Create(bass_group), Create(treble_group))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # This represents signal superposition.
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FF33FF")
        chord = Arrow(ORIGIN, (UP+RIGHT)*1.5, color="#FF33FF", buff=0)
        chord_label = Text("Chord", font_size=20, color="#FF33FF")
        chord_group = VGroup(chord, chord_label).arrange(UP)
        
        self.place_at_grid(chord_group, 'E3')
        self.play(TransformFromCopy(bass, chord), TransformFromCopy(treble, chord), FadeIn(chord_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Abstraction simplifies complex sound analysis.
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FF33FF")
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Core Constraints: The Axiomatic DNA", [
            "Spaces must pass the stress test.",
            "Closure requires staying within the set.",
            "Sum of vectors must be inside."
        ])
        
        # Polynomial Set
        poly_set = Rectangle(width=4, height=3, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(poly_set, "B2", "E5")
        
        # Gatekeeper
        gatekeeper = Dot(radius=0.3, color="#FF5733")
        self.place_at_grid(gatekeeper, "A6")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(poly_set), GrowFromCenter(gatekeeper))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF5733")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Valid sum operation
        vec_sum = VGroup(Dot(color="#33FF57"), Dot(color="#33FF57")).arrange(RIGHT)
        self.place_at_grid(vec_sum, "C3")
        self.play(FadeIn(vec_sum))
        self.play(gatekeeper.animate.set_color("#33FF57"))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#33FF57")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Invalid sum operation (outside box)
        invalid_sum = VGroup(Dot(color="#FF3333"), Dot(color="#FF3333")).arrange(RIGHT)
        self.place_at_grid(invalid_sum, "F1")
        self.play(FadeIn(invalid_sum))
        self.play(gatekeeper.animate.set_color("#FF3333"))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF3333")

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion: The Power of Abstraction", [
            "Abstraction unifies physics and engineering.",
            "We use familiar algebraic tools.",
            "Data points obey these same rules."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Start with a single Arrow vector
        vector = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*1.5, color="#FF5733")
        self.place_at_grid(vector, 'C3')
        self.play(Create(vector))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF5733")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Rapidly zoom out to reveal a vast cloud of data points
        dots = VGroup(*[Dot(point=np.random.uniform(-1, 1, 3), color="#3357FF") for _ in range(50)])
        self.place_in_area(dots, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.5)
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(vector),
            Create(dots),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#3357FF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Fade in a unified structure overlay
        overlay = VGroup(*[Line(dots[i].get_center(), dots[(i+1)%50].get_center(), color=WHITE, stroke_width=1) for i in range(50)])
        self.add(overlay)
        self.play(FadeIn(overlay))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)

outline.topic: The Logic of Abstract Vector Spaces

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: From Arrows to Rules
sections.content: Briefly revisit 2D/3D vectors (arrows with length and direction). Introduce the idea that these vectors follow specific algebraic 'rules' (addition and scaling), regardless of their physical representation.
sections.example: Visual animation: A 2D arrow being stretched and rotated, transitioning into a abstract point in a coordinate grid.

sections.title: The Generalization Leap
sections.content: Define a Vector Space not by 'arrows,' but as a collection of objects (vectors) that satisfy 8 fundamental axioms (closure, associativity, identity, inverse, etc.) under addition and scalar multiplication.
sections.example: Visual: The 'Arrow' icon morphing into a 'Function' symbol (f(x)) and a 'Polynomial' (ax² + bx + c) to show these are all 'vectors' in their own spaces.

sections.title: Application: The Library of Sounds
sections.content: Demonstrate that an abstract vector space can represent audio signals. An audio clip is a vector where each point in time is a dimension. Adding two clips creates a new 'vector' (superposition).
sections.example: Animation: A sound wave represented as a giant vector. Two characters, 'Bass' and 'Treble', are added together to create a complex musical chord vector.

sections.title: Core Constraints: The Axiomatic DNA
sections.content: Emphasize that for a set to be a vector space, it must pass the 'Stress Test': Scaling a vector must stay within the set, and adding two must stay within the set (Closure).
sections.example: Visual: A 'Gatekeeper' character checking if a set of polynomials satisfies the rules. If a sum leaves the set, the gate stays shut.

sections.title: Conclusion: The Power of Abstraction
sections.content: Summarize that abstract vector spaces allow us to solve complex problems in physics, AI, and engineering using the same familiar math we use for 2D arrows.
sections.example: Visual: A rapid zoom-out from an arrow to a cloud of data points, showing they all obey the same unified algebraic structure.
